scope: Changed compaction code and related provider, cancellation, context estimation, output preparation and automatic policy paths in both repositories.
Broader Python source audit for cross-object private access and ownership boundaries; no blanket clean-code certification of every module.
No changes to inference kernels, server protocols or cache payload formats. Metal, SSD streaming and distributed inference were not retested.
corrections: ProviderRequest owns event-handler adaptation. Cancellation no longer rebuilds already expanded messages and duplicates tool attachment companions; ordinary and structured regression tests failed before the fix and pass afterward.
RequestBudget owns lossless source splitting and checks each complete wrapped request rather than assuming additive token costs.
ToolOutputPreparer owns the choice of a shorter file representation; OutputCandidate owns updating its presentation while retaining the original source.
Budget admission and UI context observation use the same complete structured-schema and thinking-aware estimate.
Structured responses remember authoritative totals just like ordinary responses; sampled skill checkpoints require compatible thinking and an unstructured prompt.
Automatic policy compares content snapshots: equivalent restored messages do not rearm it, while edited or new messages do.
remaining_limits: An oversized protected system/user input cannot be made reducible without changing user content; compaction is attempted and the request then fails explicitly.
Budget checks depend on the supplied estimator and discovered capacity. The live test validates exact counts for this model and scenario, not every provider or multimodal format.
The full-suite coverage gate excludes the pre-existing coverage omit lists; live scenarios are opt-in and are reported separately.
